title: MTSD launches long-range facilities master planning process
text:
Schools
MTSD launches long-range facilities master planning process
The Mequon-Thiensville School District has started a long-range facilities master planning process, the district announced.
The Mequon-Thiensville School District announced it has launched a Long-Range Facilities Master Planning Process, according to the district's October family newsletter posted Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026.
The process will examine instructional spaces and capacity, including how classrooms and shared spaces support modern teaching practices, the district said. It will also evaluate building capacity and section needs, such as spatial capacity at Oriole Lane, using updated demographic data, according to the district.
The planning effort includes capital maintenance work, with the district creating what it calls a predictable 10-year maintenance plan to maintain building mechanical systems such as HVAC, electrical and plumbing, along with structural envelopes and safety infrastructure, the district said.
The district also said it will model adaptable financial scenarios intended to ensure operational stability across school environments as part of a fiscal sustainability component. Additionally, the planning process will integrate high school athletic facility planning into the district's broader districtwide facility schedule, according to the district.
Separately, the newsletter included results from the district's 2026 September Family Survey. The district said it achieved an overall Net Promoter Score of 55, matching last year's rating, with elementary families accounting for 60% of all responses. According to the district, 86% of new families enrolled because of the district's academic reputation, 93% reported their children feel safe at school, 88% felt well-prepared and welcomed before day one, and 85% of families transitioning to new buildings felt orientation eased the move.
The newsletter also noted that 2027-28 school year calendars have been approved, according to the district.
Source: Wilson Elementary School, https://wilson.mtsd.k12.wi.us/index.php?pageID=smartSiteFeed&psqFeed=true&articleID=94611391
